title: observability: token-level KV cache metrics, cost/latency breakdowns, dashboards + alert tuning
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Customers running high-throughput streaming workloads were seeing unpredictable per-token unit costs when KV cache hit rates fluctuated. We lacked visibility into token-level KV cache behavior and its direct impact on cost/latency. This PR introduces token-level KV cache metrics, integrates cost and latency breakdowns into existing inference dashboards, and tunes alerts to reduce noisy paging while catching regressions early. Changes include: 1) New metrics emitted from the serving runtime: kv_token_cache_hits, kv_token_cache_misses, kv_token_cache_hit_rate, token_cost_estimate_per_request, token_latency_breakdown (p50/p90/p99). Metrics include dimensions: model_name, model_version, region, route, and cache_tier. 2) Tracing spans updated to include kv_cache_decision and token_cost_estimate as span attributes for sampled requests. 3) Dashboard: a new sub-dashboard under "Inference / Token-level" with panels for cache hit/miss heatmap, cost-per-token trend by route, and latency breakdown per token bucket. 4) Alert tuning: added two primary alerts - TokenLevelCacheDrop (fires when kv_token_cache_hit_rate drops >20% vs 1h baseline with sustained drop for 10m) and TokenCostSpike (fires when token_cost_estimate_per_request increases >30% vs 30m baseline). Alerts are scoped by route and region and use increased thresholds in non-prod. 5) Backfill and migration: included a migration to create aggregated daily rollups for historical dashboards and an exporter script to resample 7 days of metrics for new panels. Verification: unit tests for metric emitters, integration test against local observability stack, manual dashboard QA on staging using replayed traffic. Rollout plan: deploy metrics emitter behind a feature flag, enable dashboards in staging, enable alerts in staging for 48h with ops on-call, then promote to prod with gradual alert activation (staged by region). Related: ENG-9042 (KV cache visibility), ENG-9101 (cost attribution).

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Nice work. A few nits on labels and metric cardinality — can we ensure we only tag by route and model, not by request_id?
Maya Chen: Good call, removed request_id from dimensions and added a dedicated example for low-cardinality tags.
Lena García: The TokenLevelCacheDrop alert looks sensible but I worry about bursty workloads. Can we use a longer lookback for models with small sample counts?
Maya Chen: Added adaptive thresholding using sample_count > 100 as a guard; fallback to longer lookback (3h) for low-sample routes.
Tom Okafor: Verified staging dashboards and the backfill script ran without errors. One comment on the rollup job memory limit — added a cap and chunking.
Ops (approval): Confirmed alert noise reduced after tuning in staging, +1 to promote to prod.
CI: lint warnings on span_attributes.go fixed in follow-up commit.
Maya Chen: Addressed lint warnings and rebased; CI green.

merge_info: Merged by Arjun Patel using squash-merge. Changelog entry added. Deployment gate: metrics emitter rolled out under feature flag and dashboard published immediately. Alerts enabled in prod after 48h staggered activation.
release_notes: Added token-level KV cache metrics and token cost/latency breakdown dashboards. New alerts: TokenLevelCacheDrop, TokenCostSpike (staged by route/region). Improves visibility into per-token unit economics and reduces noisy alerts. Toggle via feature flag: kv_token_metrics_enabled.

Validate dashboard panels show expected heatmaps and cost breakdowns
Enable alerts in staging for 48h and confirm noise is low
